title: Elijah and the Widow's Last Meal

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The prophet Elijah had told King Ahab that there would be no rain in the land, except by God's word. The drought came. For a while, Elijah lived by a brook, and ravens brought him bread and meat morning and evening. But in time the brook dried up.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Then God sent Elijah to a town called Zarephath, outside Israel, near Sidon. God told him a widow there would feed him.

verses.text: So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, the widow woman was there gathering of sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, the widow woman was there gathering of sticks: and he called to her, and said,

segments.speaker: elijah
segments.text: Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Water was precious in a drought. Still, she went to get it. As she was going, Elijah called after her and asked her to bring a piece of bread as well.

verses.text: And she said, As the LORD thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.

segments.speaker: widow
segments.text: As the LORD thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: This is one of the saddest sentences in the Bible. She was gathering a few sticks to cook one last small meal for herself and her son. After that, she expected them both to starve. She was not being unkind to the stranger. She simply had nothing left to give.

verses.text: And Elijah said unto her, Fear not; go and do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son.

segments.speaker: elijah
segments.text: Fear not; go and do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son.

verses.text: For thus saith the LORD God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the LORD sendeth rain upon the earth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For thus saith the LORD God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the LORD sendeth rain upon the earth.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Fear not. Elijah asked her to do something very hard: to make him a small cake first, and then make something for herself and her son. He told her what God had said, that her flour and oil would not run out until the rain came again.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Imagine standing in her kitchen. Her son was hungry. There was barely enough for one meal. And a stranger from another country was asking her to trust the word of his God.

verses.text: And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days.

verses.text: And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by Elijah.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by Elijah.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: She did what Elijah said. And it happened just as God had spoken through him. Day after day, she reached into the barrel and found enough flour. Day after day, there was oil in the jar. Not a great store of food. Just enough, each day, for the prophet, for the widow and for her son.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: This story is about God's care for a poor widow and her child in a foreign land, in the middle of a drought. She was not an Israelite. She was not wealthy or powerful. But God sent his prophet to her house and kept her family through the hard season.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: It does not promise that every empty cupboard will be filled. It tells what God did for one widow, one jar and one barrel. It shows a God who saw a mother in Zarephath gathering sticks for what she thought was her last meal.

cultural.note: The widow is poor but never pitiable or comic; a foreign woman honoured.
